stories.title: Electric car registrations surge 76 percent in October
stories.summary: Electric passenger vehicle registrations reached 37,049 units in October 2026, a 76.47 percent increase year-on-year. FADA data shows electric cars accounted for 7.3 percent of total passenger vehicle registrations, doubling their share from the previous year. This growth occurred despite a 14.23 percent decline in the overall passenger vehicle market.

stories.title: Odisha proposes 290 new EV charging stations
stories.summary: The Government of Odisha has proposed 290 public EV charging stations under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. The plan targets 13 cities and various highway corridors to build a robust EV ecosystem. State officials announced the proposal on November 3, 2026, to accelerate green mobility across the region.

stories.summary: Electric commercial vehicle retail sales reached 4,942 units in October 2026, a 162.3 percent increase year-on-year. FADA data indicates this growth pushed market penetration to 4.29 percent, up from 1.67 percent in October 2025. Tata Motors and Euler Motors led the volume charts for the month.

stories.title: SoundHound AI and Ultraviolette partner for voice-controlled bikes
stories.summary: SoundHound AI and Ultraviolette Automotive are integrating voice AI into electric motorcycles. Shown at EICMA 2026, the technology allows riders to control safety settings and diagnostics via helmet headsets. The companies claim this partnership aims to set new industry standards for human-machine interaction in electric two-wheelers.

stories.title: Tata Motors acquires 89.42 percent stake in Iveco
stories.summary: Tata Motors completed the acquisition of an 89.42 percent stake in Iveco Group for approximately 3.43 billion euros on October 30, 2026. The combined commercial vehicle enterprise reports revenue of 21 billion euros. Tata Motors is now exploring the assembly of selected Iveco vehicles within India.

stories.title: Tata Motors increases stake in Iveco Group
stories.summary: Tata Motors subsidiary TML CV Holdings has reached a 96.29% stake in Iveco Group following a tender offer. The move follows the companies' recent announcement of a global commercial mobility partnership. The tender offer for the additional shares was valued at approximately EUR 263.65 million.

stories.title: Tata Motors and Iveco Group form global mobility enterprise
stories.summary: Tata Motors and Iveco Group have launched a joint enterprise to compete across global markets and technology cycles. The companies describe the venture as a global commercial mobility enterprise with the scale and capabilities to grow across markets. The entity combines industrial heritage with complementary product portfolios.

stories.title: Mahindra heavy vehicle capacity hits 100%
stories.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra is planning capacity additions for heavy commercial vehicles after demand for its Blazo i-TRK line pushed factory utilization to 100%. The company reported a 37% volume increase in Q2 FY27 for its commercial division. It is currently executing the merger of SML Mahindra.

stories.title: Carraro India forecasts 23% annual growth for 4WD tractors
stories.summary: Carraro India projects the domestic 4WD tractor market will grow at a 23% compound annual rate to 600,000 units by 2029. The company claims a 50% share of non-captive agricultural 4WD axle volumes above 40 HP. It reported raw-material localisation of 79.9% in Q2 FY27.

stories.title: Michelin launches fuel-efficient truck tyre in India
stories.summary: Michelin has launched the X Multi Energy Z2, a truck and bus tyre developed for Indian operating conditions. The company claims the tyre lowers the total cost of ownership by combining fuel efficiency and robustness. Fuel accounts for approximately 50% of a fleet's overall expenditure.

stories.title: Tyre industry body seeks duty-free rubber imports
stories.summary: The Automotive Tyre Manufacturers' Association is seeking duty-free imports of natural rubber as domestic prices reach 300 rupees per kilogram. The full details of the request are unavailable as the source page is restricted to subscribers.

stories.title: Apollo Tyres expects stable European operations next year
stories.summary: Apollo Tyres expects stable European operations by the next financial year following the closure of its Enschede plant. The company is currently dismantling the facility and expects replacement manufacturing supply to be ready within two quarters. Agri and off-highway tyre supply should stabilise next year.

stories.title: Bosch India reports higher quarterly profit
stories.summary: Bosch's India unit reported a higher quarterly profit, citing increased demand for automotive parts. The full details of the financial performance are available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: SPR Auto reports 60% of business insulated from powertrain shifts
stories.summary: SPR Auto Technologies reported that 60% of its business is relatively insulated from powertrain technology shifts, with powertrain-agnostic products contributing over 35% of revenue. Consolidated total income rose 61% to 1.67 billion rupees in Q2 FY27. EBITDA margins reached 17.9%.

stories.title: SPR Auto to supply ABS parts from April
stories.summary: SPR Auto expects to begin supplying precision-plastic parts for two-wheeler anti-skid braking systems by April. The company established a new facility in Neemrana to handle the programme. Management reported that capacity utilisation was 75% to 80% before a recent 30% to 35% increase in demand.

stories.title: Uno Minda invests 85 crore in sunroof production
stories.summary: Uno Minda has approved 85 million rupees for sunroof manufacturing to expand capacity at its Bawal plant by Q2 FY28. The investment is part of a broader cycle focused on premiumisation and electric mobility. The company is currently testing whether new product lines generate stronger margins.

stories.title: Lucknow sees luxury car spending spree
stories.summary: Luxury car sales in Lucknow surged during the Dhanteras period, with 2,500 vehicles sold between 20 October and 6 November. Sales included four cars priced above 20 million rupees. The most expensive unit sold was a BMW X6 for 28.6 million rupees.

stories.title: Automakers target 58,000 deliveries for Dhanteras
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai and Tata Motors expected to deliver over 58,000 vehicles on Dhanteras. Mahindra & Mahindra reported strong demand and near-zero SUV inventory. Automakers are reporting higher retail sales across the festive period, with Hyundai targeting a 14% increase in units compared to last year.

stories.title: Maruti Suzuki expects 30,000 deliveries on Dhanteras
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki expects to deliver 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras following a 36% year-on-year growth in retail deliveries through Dussehra. The company reported its highest-ever monthly wholesale volume of 276,000 units in October. Nearly half of all bookings were for CNG-powered models.

stories.title: Dealership franchise activity continues
stories.summary: Recent data shows five Chevrolet stores were sold and 35 franchises changed hands. The full report on dealership buy-sell activity is available to subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Dealers anticipate record festive deliveries
stories.summary: Car dealers are counting on record deliveries between Dhanteras and Diwali to reduce inventory levels. Passenger vehicle stocks remained at 43 to 45 days in October. The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations expects inventories to fall below 30 days by the end of December.

stories.title: Auto dealers report positive sentiment despite EV constraints
stories.summary: Automobile dealers report strong demand across segments for the festive season, though supply constraints in electric vehicles may limit some deliveries. The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations noted that market sentiment remains positive, with dealers expecting sales growth to continue through November.

stories.title: Dealers report strong festive demand
stories.summary: Automobile dealers anticipate strong sales across all segments for Dhanteras, though EV supply constraints may limit some deliveries. Over 51% of dealers expect sales growth in November. The pre-owned car market is also seeing high demand, with supply currently outstripping interest.

stories.title: Axis Bank launches 30-minute auto loan disbursement
stories.summary: Axis Bank has launched a digital auto loan service for car and two-wheeler buyers, promising loan disbursement in as little as 30 minutes. The platform integrates vehicle selection, approval, and authorization into a single digital journey. The bank says it is designed to simplify the vehicle financing experience.

stories.title: Maruti Suzuki to build 12 automated driving test tracks in Telangana
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki has signed an agreement with the Telangana government to establish 12 automated driving test tracks across six locations. The project, part of the company's corporate social responsibility initiative, aims to reduce human intervention and introduce technology-driven assessments for driving licences. The tracks were announced on November 5.

stories.title: ADAS technology faces data hurdles on Indian roads
stories.summary: Thyssenkrupp executives say advanced driver assistance systems must be trained on country-specific driving behaviour to function effectively. The technology requires large volumes of real-world data to navigate India's complex traffic conditions. ADAS performance remains dependent on the interaction between motorists, road infrastructure, and the surrounding environment.

stories.summary: Taiwanese developer Turing Drive is focusing on autonomous software for low-speed electric shuttles and golf-style carts. The company has logged over 30,000 kilometers across 10 global deployment sites. Unlike major automotive manufacturers, the firm scales its open-source autonomy stack primarily through partnerships with vehicle manufacturers.

stories.summary: Bosch is exhibiting driver assistance, AI cockpits, and robotic sensing at the 9th China International Import Expo. stories.summary: Indian Railways inaugurated its first indigenous hydrogen-powered train on 17 July 2026. The locomotive generates electricity onboard using hydrogen fuel cell technology. The train is currently operating on the Jind-Sonipat section of the Northern Railway as part of a push toward sustainable rail mobility.

stories.title: China clean-tech machine and global climate
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Reuters reports on the role of China in the global climate fight through its clean-tech manufacturing capabilities. The industry continues to reshape international markets as production scales up to meet global demand for renewable energy and electric vehicle components.

stories.title: Texas Instruments on the software defined vehicle
stories.summary: Texas Instruments describes its role as providing the bricks to the architects of modern vehicles. The company says it supplies the technology for digital clusters, ABS systems and central computers to help OEMs execute their visions. The car is now a computer on wheels.

stories.title: Toyota overtakes Nissan in Japanese EV sales
stories.summary: Toyota has overtaken Nissan to lead the Japanese electric vehicle market for the first full year. Sales data indicates a shift in the domestic landscape as the two manufacturers compete for market share in a segment that remains a small portion of total vehicle sales.

stories.title: Seres and Li Auto prepare for European debut
stories.summary: Weak demand in China is pushing more electric vehicle makers into Europe. Seres Group and Li Auto are planning debuts on the continent in 2027 to chase the overseas gains seen by BYD. Domestic sales have stalled, so the manufacturers are looking elsewhere.

stories.title: Tesla leads European electric car sales
stories.summary: Battery-electric vehicle sales in Europe increased by 60 percent in September 2026 to 416,433 units. The Tesla Model Y and Model 3 were the top-selling electric models and the best-selling cars overall. The total European new car market expanded by 10.2 percent.

stories.title: European electric car sales grow in 2026
stories.summary: Battery-electric vehicle sales in Europe increased by 41.9 percent to 2,549,810 units in the first three quarters of 2026. All-electric cars now account for almost a quarter of the total market. Volkswagen remains the top-selling brand, despite losing market share.

stories.title: German automotive sentiment improves
stories.summary: Business sentiment among German car manufacturers improved in October, according to the ifo economic institute. The industry remains optimistic about future conditions despite BMW reporting a profit slump and weak sales in China. Optimism is currently being tested by financial results.

stories.title: Volkswagen retains top spot in European market
stories.summary: New passenger vehicle registrations in Europe increased by 10.2 percent in September 2026. Volkswagen remains the best-selling carmaker, despite losing market share and volume. Battery electric vehicles reached a 29.9 percent market share in the EU. The Tesla Model Y was the top-selling model.

stories.title: Japan EV market share reaches 4.6 percent
stories.summary: Japan recorded 14,644 electric vehicle sales in October, capturing a 4.6 percent market share. Toyota has overtaken Nissan to secure the lead for the first full year. The transition to electric power continues to move at its own pace.

stories.title: European electric vehicle share reaches 34 percent
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Reports indicate that battery-electric vehicle market share in Europe reached 34 percent in October, with Germany setting a new record for the region. The data reflects ongoing shifts in European consumer preferences for electric transport.
